collection.description: It's been so hot for so long that a villager has given up on everything except lying in a hammock.

ask.text:
It's been so hot for so long that (name) has given up on everything except lying in a hammock. (He/She) loves lying in a hammock. (He/She) has always loved it. But this summer (he/she) has done it so much that the hammock has worn a groove in each palm, and the other villagers have started leaving their chores at the foot of the hammock as a hint.
This morning there is a pile of baskets, a broken spear and a goat. The goat is looking at (him/her). Should (name) get up and do the chores, or roll over and ignore the goat?

c1o1.text: By the time (he/she) has finished the pile, (name) has found out (he/she) rather likes being busy. When (he/she) goes back to the hammock that evening, it feels strangely dull. (He/She) lies there for a minute, gets up again, and goes to see if anyone needs help with supper. The hammock hangs empty for the rest of the summer, and the goat moves into it.

c1o2.text: The goat does not want to be milked. It kicks the bucket over, kicks (name), and finally sits on (him/her). By the time (name) gets out from under it, (he/she) has made up (his/her) mind about work for good: it is a trap, and the goat is in on it. "I got up once," (he/she) says darkly, climbing back into the hammock. "Look where it got me."

c1.text: (Name) groans, swings (his/her) legs out of the hammock and starts on the pile. The baskets first, then the spear, then the goat, which turns out to need milking...

c2o1.text: The goat stands there all day. It stands there all night. In the morning it is still there, chewing slowly, staring. (Name) cracks. (He/She) gets up and works through the whole pile, the baskets, the spear and the goat, and finds, to (his/her) annoyance, that the worst part of work was lying in the hammock thinking about it. The goat follows (him/her) everywhere after that, as if to make sure.

c2o2.text: The goat starts chewing on the hammock rope. (Name) doesn't notice until the rope gives way and (he/she) lands on (his/her) back in the dust with a thump that knocks the breath out of (him/her). After that, (he/she) can't relax in a hammock, or on a mat, or anywhere at all, without listening for chewing.

c2.text: (Name) rolls over to face the other way. The goat walks around the hammock and looks at (him/her) from the other side...
